label: Antonio da Vinci
summary: Paternal grandfather of Leonardo. His family note records Leonardo's birth on 15 April 1452, and his 1457 catasto declaration lists Leonardo in his household.

claims.statement: A transcription of his 1457 catasto declaration reports that he gave his age as 85, which implies birth about 1372. An age in a tax return is not a birth record.

sources.cite: Università di Firenze repository (FLORE), Intervento Colombaria, PDF on the da Vinci family tax declarations. Seen in a web search result summary only; the page was not opened in this session.

claims.statement: Usually said to have died about 1465. No document was found in this round.

sources.cite: Standard biographies. Model recall, not checked in this session.

check_in: later catasto returns of the family (1469)

claims.statement: In a family notebook (a protocol that had belonged to his grandfather ser Guido) Antonio recorded: 'Nacque un mio nipote, figliuolo di ser Piero mio figliuolo, a dì 15 d'aprile in sabato a ore 3 di notte. Ebbe nome Lionardo', followed by the baptism and the names of godparents. Reported as found by Emil Möller in 1931 to 1933.

sources.cite: Museo Galileo, Leonardo itinerary, Childhood. Seen in a web search result summary only; the page was not opened in this session.
Gingko Edizioni, Was Leonardo da Vinci really born on 15 April 1452 at 3 am? Seen in a web search result summary only; the page was not opened in this session.

value.text: '3 di notte' is Italian hours, counted from sunset

claims.statement: Converting 'ore 3 di notte' to about 10 to 11 pm modern time, and the date to the Gregorian calendar, are interpretations of the note.

sources.cite: Gingko Edizioni, birth hour article. Seen in a web search result summary only; the page was not opened in this session.

claims.statement: The declaration, delivered on 28 February 1457 Florentine style (1458 modern), lists 'Lionardo figliuolo di detto ser Piero non legiptimo nato di lui e della Chaterina' aged 5 among his mouths to feed.

open_questions: Exact archival shelfmark of the protocol containing the 1452 note, and who first published it (Möller 1931 or 1933).

timeline.text: Grandfather. Recorded Leonardo's birth in a family note and listed him in his household in the catasto of 1457. The end of the bar is an estimate of his death.
